s: HTTP/2 protobuf RPC framework giving typed contracts, multiplexed streams, and deadlines between services.
w: .proto files define services/messages; codegen produces typed clients/servers in dozens of languages. HTTP/2 multiplexes many concurrent calls per connection; bidirectional streaming flows naturally. Deadline metadata propagates through call chains enabling cascading cancellation. Load balancing works L7 (per-RPC) via proxy or client-side aware balancers.
use: Internal microservice meshes needing efficient typed contracts
Polyglot environments sharing single schema source-of-truth
Streaming use cases: live telemetry, chat relays, chunked uploads
avoid: Public partner APIs where REST/JSON ubiquity lowers friction
world: Google's entire internal RPC fabric (Stubby ancestor)

pat.d: Deadline failures feed breaker stats naturally per-endpoint.

pits: Proto field-number reuse corrupting payloads - reserved tags discipline
TCP head-of-line blocking at L4 - HTTP/3/gRPC future mitigations
tips: Deadline propagation story (why one slow leaf shouldn't eat whole budget) is interview gold
